01 · Choose your helpers

Module settings

Open Configure Settings → Region Spell Automation → Open Module Options. GMs manage world options; players can change their client options. Previous settings carry over.

  1. Choose the relevant tab: Regions, Targeting, Rolls & Damage, Effects, Chat, Weapon Mastery & Attack Properties, or GM NPC & Damage.
  2. Enable the options your table wants. Damage prompts, damage application, effects, NPC saves, and card presentation are separate choices.
  3. Click Save Options. Switching tabs preserves draft changes; Cancel leaves stored settings unchanged.

Keep an active GM connected for automatic application and Region setup. Enable overlapping targeting, damage, or mastery automation in only one module while testing.

02 · From spell to living Region

Add a spell Region

Use an existing spell from the SRD, Foundry Player's Handbook, or a D&D Beyond import. The module uses that item's activities and effects; it does not create a replacement spell.

  1. Prepare your spell or feature

    Its casting activity must create a D&D5e Region. Add the recurring save or damage activities and existing effects you need to the same item.

  2. Open the manager

    Use Compendiums → Open Region Spell Manager, or open the Spell and Region Manager from Module Options. Choose Edit beside an existing configuration, or add a new one.

  3. Drop in your item

    Choose Add New Spell / Feature Region. Drag a spell, player feature, or monster ability from an actor sheet, Items, or a compendium into the drop window.

  4. Configure, save, and cast

    Match activity names exactly and choose entry, exit, movement, turn-start, or turn-end triggers with the appropriate targeting mode.

    Add conditions or existing Region Effects. Consider Once Per Turn and Share Activity Card Per Turn for repeated areas, or Movement Damage increments for Spike Growth.

    Click Confirm / Save, enable the configuration in the manager, and test a fresh cast after each change.

Start/end-turn triggers require active combat and initiative. Once Per Turn means once per target in the current combat turn, not once per round. Shared cards can gain new targets and reuse the damage already rolled.

03 · Keep targets connected

Confirm and retarget

Enable Auto Target and Confirm Spell/Feature Regions. Place the area: automatic selection follows the card's enemy/ally targeting relative to the caster, with a matching configured trigger as fallback, then everyone eligible.

  1. Review Confirm Targets. Target tokens on the map to add them; click a listed name to remove it.
  2. Confirm to update the activity card and continue to saves and damage. Close — Resolve Manually leaves the cast available for manual resolution.
  3. To correct a card later, select the intended tokens and click Retarget. Weapon and attack cards are supported too.

After Shield or another AC change, Retarget refreshes linked hit/miss results without replacing the original dice. It does not undo applied damage. Linked concentration removes the area when concentration ends; instantaneous areas clear at the caster's turn end.

End linked concentration from the token HUD

Enable Show End Concentration on Token HUD, then right-click the concentrating token. As the GM or actor owner, use the End Concentration control to end concentration quickly. Regions linked to the originating spell are removed automatically.

04 · Keep the original dice

Advantage, normal
& disadvantage

  1. Enable Adjust Saving Throw Advantage and/or Adjust Attack Roll Advantage.
  2. Hover over a completed save or attack result and select ADV / NORMAL / DISADV.
  3. The original d20 and bonuses remain. An additional d20 rolls only when needed, then stays cached for later changes.

Linked results update, but damage already rolled or applied is not reversed. For supported damage formulas, enable Adjust Damage Normal / Critical and use the result's NORMAL / CRITICAL controls. Complex or modified formulas may require manual correction.

Normal and critical damage

Enable Adjust Damage Normal / Critical, hover over a damage result, and select NORMAL / CRITICAL. Base dice and bonuses stay in place; Critical adds only the extra dice required, then reuses cached results on later changes. Damage already applied is not undone. Complex or modified formulas may require manual correction.

05 · Resolve through native cards

Damage and effects

Configure these independent options to suit your table. Effects must already be assigned to the activity.

  • Prompt Damage after an Attack Hit: opens the native damage dialog on a confirmed hit, retaining critical and weapon-mode information. Unknown hit results remain manual.
  • Prompt Damage for Save Activities: opens the native dialog for saves with damage; area casts wait for target confirmation.
  • Auto Apply Damage: applies through the native damage tray. Attacks use confirmed hits; save damage waits for every eligible target's result. Native multipliers, resistance, immunity, and vulnerability remain in use.
  • Automatically Apply Buffs: applies existing effects from non-rolling Utility activities to the caster or eligible recorded targets.
  • Auto Apply Saved Effects: failed saves receive assigned effects; successful saves receive those marked On Save. With auto damage enabled, effects follow damage.
  • Autoapply Status on Hit: applies assigned attack effects to hit targets, independently of auto damage.
  • Automatically Roll GM NPC Saves: uses native fast-forward rolls for NPCs without player owners. PCs and player-owned NPCs retain prompts.

Native effect application handles duration, concentration, and scaling. Interacting with relevant card controls or applying damage manually stops that activity's automatic damage workflow.

06 · Your weapon's mastery

Weapon masteries

  1. Unlock the weapon's mastery on the actor using D&D5e's native Weapon Mastery configuration.
  2. Enable Effect Automation: Weapon Masteries in Module Options → Weapon Mastery & Attack Properties. Keep a GM connected.
  3. Use the weapon's mastery on the normal attack. Sap applies on hits; Vex and Slow apply after damage. Use card actions for Topple saves and Graze miss damage.

Sap/Vex controls allow corrections, and the next roll's mode can still be changed. Graze creates a damage card; application follows your chosen damage workflow. Push, Nick, and Cleave remain manual.

07 · Correct an application

Undo damage
and effects

  1. As GM, find the source card after a tracked application.
  2. Click Undo Damage to reverse that card's recorded HP, temporary HP, and temporary maximum HP changes. Multiple applications from the same card reverse together.
  3. Click Undo Effect to remove effects created by the card or restore refreshed effects, independently of HP. Changes superseded by a later cast are preserved.
  4. The corresponding tray reopens for manual application. Original dice and other cards remain unchanged.

Undo requires recorded applications made after the feature loaded; older history cannot be reconstructed. Keep a GM connected to record player applications.
